transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um, I came in because I just barely sleep right anymore. I'll just lie there at night... hearing the rain, or thinking about the bluff giving way. And then when I finally do pass out, I wake up all sweaty from these dreams. It's just messing me up because I end up showing up to my shift at the call center feeling like I never even slept.
Has the bluff actually given way or caused some kind of dangerous incident that you experienced firsthand, or is it more that you've been worried about it happening?
Yeah, it actually happened. The bluff trail collapsed while I was out there, and I got trapped. Um, so this whole thing has been going on for about four months, basically ever since that happened.
Since the bluff collapse, have you noticed yourself avoiding places or situations that remind you of it, or having sudden distressing memories or flashbacks of the event during the day?

Yeah, I definitely avoid it. I won't go anywhere near the coast trails now. I don't even like thinking about it, honestly. I've actually been dodging texts from my hiking buddies, too. Just... even talking about going out there or seeing their messages makes my chest tighten up, so I just ignore them.
Since the collapse, have you noticed yourself feeling more on edge or easily startled, like being jumpy at sudden noises or feeling like you need to stay alert to your surroundings?

Not really, no. Um... I mean, I don't think so. I don't really get jumpy at sudden noises or anything like that. I'm mostly just exhausted all day from not sleeping, but I don't feel like I need to constantly look over my shoulder or stay on high alert, if that makes sense.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient experienced a life-threatening trauma (trail collapse with entrapment) four months ago, exceeding the 1-month duration threshold that rules out Acute Stress Disorder. She reports intrusive nightmares related to the event (re-experiencing), persistent avoidance of trauma-related places and reminders (avoidance cluster), and sleep disturbance (arousal cluster), causing clear functional impairment (poor work performance due to exhaustion). Although hypervigilance/startle response is denied, sleep disturbance alone satisfies the arousal criterion. The chronicity (>1 month), direct exposure to a life-threatening event, and multi-cluster symptomatology are most consistent with PTSD rather than Adjustment Disorder or Acute Stress Disorder.
